problem: Evaluate the line integral of the function $f(x,y)=4xy$ along the ellipse $C$ with equation $4{x}^{2}+8{y}^{2}=16,$ traversed once in the counterclockwise direction.
worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s={\int }_{a}^{b}f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t.
$$

 

Note that we can write the equation of our ellipse in the form

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{(\sqrt{2})^{2}}=1.
$$

So, the curve $C$ is an ellipse centered at $O$ with horizontal and vertical semiaxes of $2$ and $\sqrt{2},$ respectively. Therefore, it can be parametrized as 

$$
r(t)=⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,0\le t\le 2\pi .
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖,$ we get following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)j \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{sin}^{2}⁡t+2{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{2{sin}^{2}⁡t+2({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\sqrt{2+2{sin}^{2}⁡t}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=4xy$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =4\cdot 2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot \sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t=8\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}4xy\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }8\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot \sqrt{2+2{sin}^{2}⁡t}\cdot \text{d}t \\  & =8\sqrt{2}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\sqrt{2+2{sin}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this using the substitution $u=2+2{sin}^{2}⁡t,$ $\text{d}u=4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}8\sqrt{2}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\sqrt{2+2{sin}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t & =2\sqrt{2}{\int }_{2}^{2}\sqrt{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\sqrt{2}\cdot \frac{2}{3}{u}^{3/2}{|}_{2}^{2} \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$
